⚠️ **TWO SURVIVED, AND THEY ARE THE SAME HOLE.** Dropping the within-piece term from either key —
so every prim and every point of one deformed piece carries the SAME number — left the suite at
**136 `[PASS]` / 0**, `output_guard_parity` included. The reason is that Houdini's `sort` happens
to be **stable** here, so equal keys kept the order `copytopoints` emitted them in, which is
already the reference's. That is luck resting on an undocumented property: the whole point of the
second term is that the key is **TOTAL**, so the answer does not depend on how the sort breaks
ties. Nothing asserted totality, so nothing could see the term go.

`piece_order_key_is_total` asserts the property directly — on a build with 30 deformed pieces
whose largest contributes 34 prims, **0 duplicate prim keys and 0 duplicate point keys out of
1 052 / 1 112** — and it is independent of the sort, of stability and of the fixture's shape. Both
mutations were re-run against it and **both are caught**. **No survivors remain.**

⚠️ **AND THE RESTORED .hda's HASH MOVED, WHICH IS A THIRD FINDING.** `12ac2248 → 7f521a91` after
restoring every mutated file. It is not a failed restore: **two consecutive rebuilds of an
UNCHANGED tree produce different bytes** (138 512 vs 138 519, differing from byte 45 onward — a
container length or timestamp, and the archive is compressed so everything shifts). Structurally
the two are the same asset: **61 nodes, every node's type, every input wire and every parameter's
raw value identical**, compared through HOM rather than through a digest. §25 recorded the .hda as
"byte-identical before and after three rebuilds", and the committed file was indeed unchanged
across `935d2ef`…`b15a338` — so this is either new to this build or was previously masked. Either
way **a hash is not a valid A/B oracle for this asset**; the network comparison is. **D240.**

### 26.7 D25's warning, and the station table it needed

`_bend_deviation` is the one warning only a DEFORMED piece can raise, and without it the native
branch ships an element the reference stamps `pc_warn_bend_resolution` on and it does not — which
`output_guard_parity` reads as a missing PRIM ATTRIBUTE on the whole build. It is computed in
`pc_deform_gate`, which already holds the span and the verdict, from `pc_kit_meta`'s per-module
station table.

⚠️ **THE TABLE STORES THE RAW LOCAL x, NOT `x - ax`.** A point's `P` is float32 and the difference
of two float32s is not one, so writing the difference into an array attribute would quantise the
very numbers the deform is built on. The consumer subtracts `ax` itself, in 64 bits, exactly as
`place._stations` does — and the dedupe is unaffected, since `(x2 - ax) - (x1 - ax)` is `x2 - x1`.
The LAST run of a repeated `pc_name` wins, which is `Kit._by_name`'s rule and `copytopoints`'
`useidattrib`'s.

### 26.8 The ceilings: two tables, because the shape decides the cost

`WRANGLE_CEILING_US` is recorded on a STRAIGHT run where every piece stays packed. Five of the
asset's 23 wrangles never cook there, and four more see the module's whole polygon soup instead of
one prim per piece — so folding a deformed shape into it would move eighteen recorded rows by the
prim-to-piece ratio and guard neither shape. `WRANGLE_DEFORM_CEILING_US` is the deformed shape's
own table, same recipe, same two sizes, over a 0.6 m ripple at 4 466 and 17 852 pieces:

| node | deformed µs/piece | straight µs/piece | ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pc_deform` | 0.5755 – 0.5890 | — | 1.53 |
| `pc_deform_prep` | 0.1023 – 0.1059 | — | 0.32 |
| `pc_kit_meta` | 0.0451 – 0.0665 | — | 0.22 |
| `pc_kit_rank` | 0.0119 – 0.0129 | — | 0.09 |
| `pc_piece_key` | 0.2171 – 0.2325 | — | 0.64 |
| `pc_deform_gate` | 0.9103 – 1.0080 | 0.2355 – 0.2533 | 2.58 |
| `pc_warn_collate` | 1.5846 – 1.6232 | 0.2358 – 0.2490 | 4.12 |
| `pc_finalize` | 0.3030 – 0.3214 | 0.1119 – 0.1279 | 0.86 |

⚠️ **THE TWO MOST EXPENSIVE NODES ON A DEFORMED BUILD ARE NOT WRANGLES, so no ceiling row guards
them.** At 17 852 pieces / ~304 000 prims, `pc_order` (the sort) is **125–131 ms** and `pc_pieces`
(the merge) 24–28 ms. On the 20 km ripple that is 130 ms of a 1 007 ms cook — the second-largest
item after `pc_plan_solve`'s 568 ms. That is the price of putting `place.build`'s job order back
together and it is recorded here so nobody rediscovers it as a surprise. **D231**: if a cheaper
ordering exists it is worth a cycle, but the sort is correct and the correctness is not
negotiable.

⚠️ **`deform_wrangle_rig_really_deforms` ASSERTS HALF, NOT ALL, AND THE HALF IS D27.** The starter
kit alternates `post` (rigid) with `panel`, and `_needs_deform` returns False on a rigid module
before it measures anything — so a ripple no module can chord still leaves every post packed
(8 925 of 17 852). What the row asserts is that all five deform-branch nodes COOKED.

### 26.9 13.9 N6's deciding experiment, committed

Conform is the largest refused class left by 4.5x, so the next cycle's first question is whether
N6 is a PORT of the drape's numbers or a REWRITE of them. That is one measurement, and it is
`conform_drop_is_portable_to_vex`.

`conform.Surface.drop` is `hou.Geometry.intersect` twice (down-axis, then back no further than the
hit already found, nearest wins, `tolerance = 1e-6`, `min_hit = 0.0`); `drop_many` is the `ray`
VERB, already measured bit-identical to it. A native conform is a THIRD implementation — VEX's own
`intersect()` — over 200 queries on five surfaces: an exact-tie flat sheet, a rational slope, an
IRRATIONAL slope (the committed fixtures' `y = 0.25x` is exactly representable and hid a real
divergence for a cycle, D111), a REVERSED winding (D52), and the same irrational ramp at 20 km.

**0 hit-flag mismatches, worst 1.776e-15 m. The drape is a PORT.**

⚠️ **AND THE FIRST READING OF IT SAID NO.** Compared as DOUBLES the two disagree by **3.815e-07 m**
at fixture scale and **9.375e-04 m at 20 km**, which would fail `_first_difference`'s 1e-9
rounding outright. The whole divergence is in x and z — the two components a −Y drop never moves.
VEX's `intersect` in a 64-bit wrangle hands back the query's own DOUBLE coordinates and
`hou.Geometry.intersect` hands back float32 ones, so it is D111's finding **from the other side**:
the REFERENCE is the quantised one. It disappears in the float32 `P` storage the output is
actually compared in. The condition rides with the check: read the drop off the AXIS COMPONENT and
rebuild the position from the query, exactly as `drop_many` already does.

### 26.12 Where to start the audit

**Dev-loop rule 0 is NOT discharged for this cycle.** The honest words for everything above are
"implemented, verified by the suite, not independently audited". Start here:

1. **`pc_deform.vfl` against `place._deform_positions`, line for line.** The frame transport is

   is a superset of the station tangents, and that `_transport` is the only prefix-scan in that
   function.
2. **The order key.** `_pkey0` is taken in `pc_proto`, which is upstream of `pc_place_valid`'s
   blast — check that nothing between the plan and the split can reorder points, and that a kit
   with two adjacent packed prims of the same `pc_name` cannot make two pieces' keys collide.
3. **`pc_built`'s switch.** Its selector is an `npoints()` expression on a sibling. Confirm the
   all-packed path is byte-identical to the pre-N5 build (`geometry_digest` on the 92 cases is the
   instrument) and that the expression cannot evaluate against a stale cook.
4. **The two ceiling tables.** `WRANGLE_DEFORM_CEILING_US` names eight rows and the asset has 23
   wrangles; four are in both tables. Check that no wrangle is guarded on a shape it never runs.
5. **`pc_order` at 125–131 ms.** Is the sort avoidable, and is D231 a cycle or a footnote?
6. **The conform experiment.** It compares in float32 because that is the output's storage —
   check that no consumer of a drop reads it at 64 bits before it lands there (`_bend_deviation`
   and `span_deviation` both do arithmetic on sampled positions).

### 26.13 Decisions taken this cycle (§10 continues here — D226–D230 are §24's and §25 reused
two of those numbers by accident, so this cycle starts at D231)

- **D231 — putting `place.build`'s JOB ORDER back together costs 125–131 ms, and it is the second
  largest item on a deformed cook.** The native branch builds packed prims and deformed polygons
  as two `copytopoints` streams; the reference interleaves them. `pc_order` (a `sort`) and
  `pc_pieces` (a `merge`) are 125–131 ms and 24–28 ms at 17 852 pieces / ~304 000 prims, against
  `pc_plan_solve`'s 568 ms on the same build. Recorded, not fixed. If a cheaper ordering exists it
  is worth a cycle; the sort is CORRECT and that is not negotiable.
- **D232 — a warning's COUNT is per element while its STAMP is per prim, and those were the same
  number until a piece could be more than one prim.** `place._collate_warnings` counts JOBS;
  `_stamp_bulk` writes the warning onto every prim the piece produced. `pc_warn_collate` counted
  prims, which agreed with the reference on every build the branch could previously make and read
  `pc_warn_bend_resolution:6` against `:1` the moment one could not. `_srcrank == 0` is "the first
  prim of this element" and reads 0 on a packed prim, which is the same sentence.
- **D233 — a heuristic that predicts a refusal which no longer exists is DELETED, not left
  evaluating into nothing.** Level 1's deform bound was exact, cheap and, after N5, actively
  wrong: it would have refused the 1 237 ms N5 removed. `_bend_bound`, its two `pc_cfg` operands,
  `bend_bound_ok` and the whole-curve kink walk went with it, and `pc_envelope` dropped from
  0.47–0.50 to 0.0595–0.0602 µs/piece. A dead heuristic reads exactly like a live one.
- **D234 — two measured `copytopoints` facts, both silent when wrong.** (a) With
  `transform = 0` a copy is STILL TRANSLATED to its target point (probed: local x 10 onto a target
  at 100 lands at 110), so a copy that must arrive in source-local space needs the target's `P`
  zeroed, not the toggle cleared. (b) A target attribute named in TWO `targetattribs` entries is
  applied by the LAST one only — `_pkey0` in both the prims and the points entry produced the
  point attribute, **no prim attribute at all**, no warning, and every prim key reading 0.
- **D235 — the output's ORDER is a contract, and it needs a key on BOTH classes.** `output_guard_parity`
  compares every prim in order and the entire `P` array element by element. The key is
  `_pkey0 * PC_PIECE_SPAN + <index within the piece>`, where the piece index is stamped in
  `pc_proto` (the last node upstream of the packed/deformed split that still sees plan order) and
  the within-piece index rides free off the KIT through `copytopoints`. The span is CHECKED
  (`_kit_rank_max`) and the build is refused rather than shipped permuted. Probed: `sort` by
  attribute is exact at 3.07e8 over 300 000 points; a float32 read would have quantised at 1.7e7.
- **D236 — a fixture for a LEVEL 2 refusal must be checked to REACH level 2.** The first
  `guard_deform_refusals` used a flat hairpin, which reverses by turning ~180° — a CORNER, which
  level 1 refuses outright, so the row passed while exercising nothing below `pc_envelope`. "The
  output took the reference" is satisfied just as well by level 1 refusing, so **level 1 admitting
  is a separate assertion** and the reversal has to be in the vertical plane (an overhanging
  crest: `across` reverses while the 3D turn stays under the corner threshold).
- **D237 — a cost-ceiling table is per SHAPE.** Five wrangles never cook on a straight run and four
  more see the module's whole polygon soup on a deformed one, so one table cannot guard both:
  folding a deformed shape into `WRANGLE_CEILING_US` would move eighteen recorded rows by the
  prim-to-piece ratio. `WRANGLE_DEFORM_CEILING_US` is the second table; a name in both is a node
  whose cost is shape-dependent, and a wrangle in neither is the fault.
- **D238 — 13.9 N6's drape is a PORT, and the reading is the condition.** VEX's `intersect()`
  reproduces `conform.Surface.drop` to 1.776e-15 m over 200 queries on five surfaces **in the
  float32 `P` storage the output is compared in** — but to 3.815e-07 m at fixture scale and
  9.375e-04 m at 20 km as DOUBLES, all of it in the two components a −Y drop never moves, because
  VEX returns the query's double coordinates and `hou.Geometry.intersect` returns float32 ones.
  Read the drop off the AXIS COMPONENT and rebuild from the query, as `drop_many` already does.
- **D239 — a conform benchmark whose runs are off the surface measures D53's miss path.** The
  first pass of §26.1 ran 300 streets 1 600 × 1 000 m across over `conform_bench.terrain`'s
  660 × 360 m default and reported 1 742 ms; a terrain that covers them reports 3 645 ms. Any
  conform fixture owes an assertion that the run is ON the surface.

- **D240 - the .hda is NOT byte-reproducible, so a hash is not a valid A/B oracle for it.**
  Two consecutive rebuilds of an unchanged tree differ from byte 45 onward and by seven
  bytes of total length; structurally they are the same asset (61 nodes, every type, every
  input wire and every parameter raw value identical, compared through HOM). Compare the
  NETWORK, or compare the OUTPUT - never the file.
## 27. Native network build log — cycle N-4F (the §26 audit, worked through)

**Read this first.** An independent audit of §26 returned **twenty findings**. Every one was
reproduced from a pristine `git archive HEAD` export before it was touched, and every one is closed
as a **standing check with a mutation that reddens**. Three of them were not the finding the auditor
wrote: fixing the instrument the auditor asked for immediately exposed **two further shipped
divergences on the DEFAULT path** that no check in the tree could see, and a third measurement
**contradicted the auditor's own proposed fix**. All three are recorded below as found, not as
hoped.

### 27.1 The four that shipped WRONG GEOMETRY on a build the guard admits

Each one reproduced on the pristine HEAD export, `Stage = output` against `Stage = reference`, level
1 and level 2 both admitting, no node warning on either side.

| # | what | measured on HEAD | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **`attr:<name>` at an ARRAY or DICT storage** — `pc_sections.vfl`'s "present but unreadable" test was `t == 3`, and `primattribtype` returns 3 only for an **int** array | a FLOAT array `w = (7.5, 1.0)` under `attr:w eq 0.0` built **12 `gate` prims natively against the reference's 10 `panel`**; a STRING array and a DICT did the same; `ge`, `lt` and `ne` diverged identically. **12 divergences over 4 storages x 4 operators.** The int-array control was correctly refused | `t >= 3`, with the re-probed table in the comment. **0 divergences.** D241 |

With that fixed, the reference publishes `w1`/`w2` prim attributes and the native chain publishes **nothing**: a schema divergence the guard admitted | the reader drops tokens that are not attribute names (D258) and **level 1 REFUSES any build carrying a non-empty `pc_row_warns`** (D263), with an empty-value control row proving the refusal is not a blanket one |

### 27.2 The two the FIXED INSTRUMENT found, which no finding named

⚠️ **This is the part worth reading.** Finding 1 of the audit was that `_snapshot` — the oracle
`output_guard_parity` and eleven other rows compare through — recorded point attributes **by name
only** and had no storage dimension at all. Giving it point-attribute VALUES and a real storage
dimension (`hou.Attrib.numericDataType()`, which separates fpreal32 from fpreal64 and Int32 from
Int64 where `dataType()` cannot) turned **29 of 93 cases red on the first run**:

* **every int of 3.4's stamp shipped at int64 where `place.build` declares int32.** A 64-bit wrangle
  writes `i@` at int64; `geo.addAttrib(Prim, name, 0)` is int32. `pc_elem_key`, `pc_section`,
  `pc_generated`, `pc_deformed`, `pc_corner_cut`, `pc_replaced` and every `pc_warn_*` were **twice
  the reference's storage on every admitted build**, and `dataType()` reads `attribData.Int` for
  both — so `output_guard_parity` printed "identical" over all 92 cases for the whole of §26.
* and the fix has an ORDER: `pc_warn_collate` **creates** prim attributes at cook time
  (`setprimattrib` with a name that comes from data), so with `pc_out_cast` upstream of it
  `pc_warn_bend_resolution` stayed at int64 while every other int was correct. The cast is the
  **last** node of the stage now. **D262.**

Both are exactly D223's own rule — *the storage of an attribute is part of its contract* — applied
to the OUTPUT side, which is where nothing had ever applied it.

### 27.4 The two efficiency criticals, and the one the auditor's fix did NOT fix

**(a) `pc_fill` was QUADRATIC in the anchor count, and it shipped on two MAIN-page parms.**
`pc_fill`'s twelve plan arrays are `export`, so VEX copied the whole growing plan in and out once
per gap, and an `evenly` or `marker` rule calls it once per gap. Measured on the pristine HEAD
export, a 2 km straight with `Evenly Spaced Piece = post`, guard ADMITTING:

| spacing | pieces | `Stage = output` | `Stage = reference` | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 m | 3 001 | 2.107 s | 0.103 s | **20.4x** |
| 1.0 m | 6 001 | 9.389 s | 0.161 s | **58.4x** |
| 0.5 m | 12 001 | 39.141 s | 0.330 s | **118.7x** |

Doubling the anchors QUADRUPLED the node. Fixed by giving `pc_fill` fresh local arrays and
appending after it returns — semantically identical, because `pc_fill` reads its incoming arrays
exactly once as `int entry = len(o_slot)` (**D243**) — and by hoisting the pool and the slot context
out of the per-gap call (**D244**). Same fixtures now: **1.94x / 2.47x / 2.99x**, and
`pc_plan_solve` at 4 000 anchors went **47 168 ms → 719 ms**.

**(b) `Piece Order = Random` is 3.06x, and the auditor's proposed fix accounts for 6 % of it.**
The audit attributed ~230 us/piece to `pc_random01` re-seeding MT19937 across `export int mt[]`
function boundaries and proposed inlining, saying explicitly that the magnitude was inferred and not
measured. **It was measured this cycle and the inference is wrong.** Inlining the three functions
into one and truncating the first twist to the two words `genrand_res53` actually reads (provably
identical — mt[0]' and mt[1]' depend only on words the loop has not yet written) took the whole draw
from **110 us to 98 us**, and `pc_plan_solve` under `random` from 251 ms to 217 ms. Carrying
`mt[i-1]` in a register and replacing the two-element key array with scalars took it to **184 ms**.
End to end the 2 km random build went **3.96x → 3.06x**.

⚠️ **The floor is VEX itself, and it is measured.** `init_by_array` is ~1 870 strictly sequential
array steps; a bare 1 872-iteration scalar loop in a single-threaded VEX snippet costs **45 us**,
and the whole draw 98 us, against CPython's 1–2 us of C. `pc_plan_solve`'s parallel unit is the
SECTION (D222), so one long curve runs it on ONE thread. **There is no cheaper VEX.** Getting this
row under the guard's 1.6x contract needs the draws BATCHED into a parallel wrangle, which is a
two-pass solve. **D260, and it is the honest open item of this cycle.**

Both shapes now have standing rows: `output_guard_cost` gained `evenly_2km` (2.6x ceiling, reads
2.08x) and `random_2km` (4.0x ceiling, reads 3.11x), and `guard_anchor_cost_is_linear` bounds the
per-anchor GROWTH at 1.6x (reads 0.99–1.22x) with `mutation_anchor_fill_copies_the_plan` restoring
the shipped code and blowing it. **D259.**

### 27.8 Decisions taken this cycle (§10 continues here)

- **D241 — an "is it an array" test must be `>= 3`, and `primattribsize` cannot stand in for it.**
  Re-probed on 22.0.398: `primattribtype` is 0 int, 1 float, 2 string, **3 int-array, 4 float-array,
  5 string-array, 6 dict**, and every array reports `primattribsize == 1`. The comment that stood
  above the line said "3 ARRAY" and was wrong for three of the four.
- **D242 — an introspection probe may not contain the DATUM'S OWN NAME.** Searching a whole dict's
  `json_dumps` for `"<key>": {"type": "string"` fails on every key JSON escapes. Dump a ONE-KEY dict
  instead and read the FIRST `"type": "` token: the key text leaves the question. And a type probe
  with two outcomes on a three-outcome domain is a fail-open — anything that is not a scalar is
  `!unreadable:`, never a cross-type read.
- **D243 — `export` array parameters are COPIED, so an accumulator must never be passed to a
  function called in a loop.** 118x on a MAIN-page parm, invisible to 130 [PASS] / 0. The rule
  generalises: if a VEX function takes `export T[]` and the caller is in a loop, the caller passes
  FRESH arrays and appends.
- **D244 — a hoist has more than one level.** D175 hoisted the pool out of the PIECE loop; the same
  pool was still rebuilt once per GAP. Anything that is a pure function of (rule, yclass) belongs
  outside the gap loop too.
- **D245 — measure the optimisation before crediting it.** The inline the audit proposed for
  `pc_random01` is worth 6 %, not the ~100x its framing implied, and the remaining cost is VEX's own
  single-thread floor. An inferred magnitude is not a measurement, and this document says so where
  the inference was made.
- **D246 — an oracle that compares NAMES is not an oracle.** Point attributes had no values and no
  storage in `_snapshot`; two mutations 2.0 m apart moved nothing. `hou.Attrib.numericDataType()` is
  the accessor that separates fpreal32/fpreal64 and Int32/Int64 where `dataType()` cannot.
- **D247 — a tolerance applied to BOTH sides before the subtraction is not a ceiling.** `f32()` on
  both operands turns any ceiling below half a float32 ULP into a statement about storage, not about
  agreement. Assert the RAW difference against a scale-relative bound and report the quantised one
  separately.
- **D248 — an absolute timing ceiling is a property of the MACHINE.** Calibrate against a fixed
  workload cooked in the same interleaved repetitions and assert a ratio. Measured: a 33 % swing in
  the absolute figure is a 4 % swing in the ratio.
- **D249 — a multiparm is ENUMERATED, never listed.** A hand-written `class1/attribs1/...` list has
  to be edited every time an entry is added, and it was not.
- **D250 — a stage table needs a FIXTURE per branch.** The deformed branch cannot be watched on a
  straight run, where the `pc_built` switch legitimately bypasses it.
- **D251 — a declaration its own consumer contradicts is worse than no declaration.** Delete the
  columns rather than correcting them when the assertion is uniform.
- **D252 — the citation scan must read the TEST MODULES too.** That is where the runners document
  themselves, and it is where the third unwritten-oracle citation landed. Two shapes have to be
  modelled to keep it honest: keyword-argument names, and names a `check("prefix_%s" % ...)`
  composes at runtime.
- **D253 — a SET comparison needs a size floor, and the skip that feeds it must not exclude its own
  subject.** `place_packed_parity` skipped every case with no PACKED prim, which is exactly a case
  where every piece deforms.
- **D254 — a variable assigned inside a loop holds the LAST iteration.** The "this image contains
  geometry" row measured the reference image while claiming to measure the native one. And prim
  counts do not prove geometry: compare positions.
- **D255 — a comparison that is trivially satisfied says so in its own text.** A refused build
  routes `Stage = output` to the reference, so a parity diff there compares a node with itself.
- **D256 — a refusal is proved by FORCING ITS INPUT, not by deleting its line on a fixture something
  else already refuses.** And forcing cannot prove the attribute NAME is still the one upstream
  writes, so the inputs are asserted present separately.
- **D257 — a fixture must assert the property it is named for.** `addAttrib(Prim, name, [8,1,2])` is
  a TUPLE; five rows called `iarray`/`sarray` never executed the array branch, which is how three
  storages shipped wrong under five PASSing rows. This is the project's own recorded lesson
  happening inside the fix that lesson was written for.
- **D258 — artist-authored TEXT becomes attribute NAMES, so it is input and must be validated.**
  `pc_row_warns` at the wrong storage made `place.build` raise where the native chain built happily:
  warn-never-block broken on the Python side, and parity undefined rather than merely different.
- **D259 — a cost fixture built on the DEFAULT style measures the default style.** Every cost row in
  the suite left the slot parms alone, so the two MAIN-page parms that carried a 118x and a 4.0x
  regression were unreachable by any committed check.
- **D260 — OPEN: `Piece Order = Random` is 3.06x the reference and cannot be made 1.6x in VEX.**
  `random.Random(s).random()` is ~1 870 sequential array steps and VEX's single-thread floor is
  ~24 ns a step. The fix is a two-pass solve that computes the draws in a parallel wrangle. Until
  then the row ships with a 4.0x ceiling and this entry.
- **D261 — a performance headline names its SHAPE.** `pc_plan_solve` is 85 % of a 20 km single-curve
  cook and 6 % of a 300-street one, where `pc_order` is 25–30 %.
- **D262 — the OUTPUT's integer storage is a contract too, and the cast must be the LAST node.**
  Six prim ints plus every `pc_warn_*` shipped at int64 against the reference's int32 on every
  admitted build. `pc_warn_collate` CREATES attributes at cook time, so anything upstream of it
  cannot cast them.
- **D264 — a timing ceiling that cannot be calibrated is RAISED ABOVE ITS SPREAD, not left on the
  edge of it.** `bench_guard_fallback` failed on an unmutated build at 1.81x against a 1.8 ceiling;
  the recorded spread over four runs of the same commit is 1.52 / 1.57 / 1.62 / 1.81. Both sides of
  that ratio are whole asset cooks and the extra work IS the second cook, so D248's calibrator does
  not apply — D211's rule does: raise it above the spread (2.2) and write the spread down. The
  class it exists for still fails it at 2.35x.
- **D265 — A FIX WITHOUT A FIXTURE IS NOT A FIX, and only a source mutation can tell you.**
  Reverting this cycle's own `markerData` fix at source left the suite at 144 [PASS] / 0. Every
  guard hole closed in a cycle must be re-opened at source and the suite must go red, or the
  closure is a comment. And when the fixture cannot go through the test rig, that is a fact about
  the RIG and the fixture moves to the shipped asset — it does not get dropped.
- **D263 — a channel the native chain does not read is a REFUSAL, not a silence.** `pc_row_warns`
  makes the reference publish one prim attribute per token and the native chain publishes none;
  level 1 refuses a non-empty one, and an empty-value control row proves the refusal is not blanket.

## 28. Cycle V1 — the double pillar at every corner (2026-08-24)

**Reported by Hannes, in the viewport, on the shipped defaults.** Gate PC-G1, miter mode, the
12 × 8 m rectangle, starter kit: at every corner an artist sees **two pillars of different
height** where they expect one. Measured on the shipped asset before the fix:

| what | X | Z | height | slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| corner post, two mated halves | 11.92 – 12.08 | −0.08 – 0.08 | 1.30 | `corner` |
| the run's FIRST piece | 11.94 – 12.06 | **0.08 – 0.19** | 1.20 | `default` |

The Z overlap is **exactly 0.0**. The two halves are correct — sliced on the bisector, mating
perfectly. `no_gaps_or_overlaps`, `corner_abut` and `corner_seam` all PASSED, and they were right
to: **the geometry IS closed.** Closure is not composition, and nothing in the suite asserted that
the result looks like a fence.

### 28.1 The layer diagnosis — it is (a) and (c), not (b)

**(a) THE SHIPPED STYLE. This is the proximate cause.** The parameter page shipped
`Repeating Pieces = "post panel"` with `Piece Order = In turn`, so the default run is
`post panel post panel …`. An alternating two-module unit placed in a run of even count **always**
ends with a panel and **always** opens with a post — so the leg *arriving* at a corner ends in a
panel (correct) and the leg *leaving* it opens with a post (a second pillar). The same defect fires
at a RUN END, where `Piece at the Start = "post"` caps a run whose first default piece is also a
post: measured 0.12 m, exactly one post, on `A_straight` and `DL_variant_kit`.

RailClone does not compose a fence this way. Its canonical fence makes **panels the Default and
posts Evenly-spaced** ([`railclone.md`](railclone.md) §1's slot list, §6.1's *"X Evenly = pillar
rhythm"*), precisely so that the rhythm element is anchored INSIDE the run and the run's ends
belong to whatever caps them — the Corner piece at a vertex, the Start/End piece at a spline end.

**(b) THE ENGINE — a real gap, but not this defect's cause.** The engine *cannot* express the
general case "phase a composed unit after a corner assembly", and that is worth writing down:

* `plan.choose` resolves a `sequence` as `cand[index % len(cand)]`, and `plan_section` starts
  every section's fill at `index = 0`. **There is no phase or offset control on a sequence**, on
  the page or in a payload.
* `plan.cond_subject`'s subject list has no term for *"the head of this run is already capped"*.
  `cornerAngle` is the closest and it is a different fact (the section's own turn, not what the
  neighbouring assembly supplied). A `conditional` rule picks between two modules; it cannot
  re-phase a period-2 pattern.

So a style that wants `post panel` AND one pillar at a corner is inexpressible today. **That is a
recorded gap, not a blocker** — the `evenly` slot is the general answer to "rhythm element", it is
the answer RailClone reaches for, and it is now the shipped default. Anyone who wants the phase
control anyway should add a `phase` field to `Rule` and a `section_capped` ctx subject; nothing in
this cycle depends on it.

**(c) THE FIXTURE SET. This is why it shipped.** `cases.fence_style` composes `post panel` and is
used by six straight/bend cases; `cases.corner_style` — which every one of the ~20 corner cases
uses — fills with **`panel` alone**. So *the one composition the parameter page actually shipped
was in no corner case in the suite*. 3 600 numeric checks were green on a fence with two pillars at
every corner because no fixture ever built one. This is the dev-loop's own question — *what can
this fixture NOT reach?* — answered the expensive way.

### 28.2 What changed

**D266 — the shipped default composition is RailClone's canonical fence.** On the parameter page
(`devScripts/create_pf_polychain_hda.py`):

| parm | was | is |
|---|---|---|
| `Repeating Pieces` (`slot_default`) | `post panel` | **`panel`** |
| `Evenly Spaced Piece` (`slot_evenly`) | *(empty)* | **`post`** |
| `Evenly Spacing (m)` (`evenly_spacing`) | `0.0` | **`2.0`** (the starter panel's own length) |

`Piece at the Start` / `at the End` / `at Corners` are unchanged. The page still reads as a
decision list — *"panels fill the run, posts every 2 m, a corner post at corners"* is a sentence an
art director says out loud — and both help strings now name the rule (`houdini-tool-design` §1:
the artist has to be able to steer it without reading the source).

Why the `evenly` slot rather than the fill: `plan.plan_section` places evenly anchors first and
fills the gaps between them, so the rhythm element is anchored INSIDE the run — which is the
property the composed fill could not have.

⚠️ **THE SENTENCE THAT USED TO BE HERE WAS FALSE, and it shipped inside the asset's own help
string.** It read: *"D15 keeps every anchor at least half a spacing clear of a capped end. So an
anchor can never land against a corner assembly or a start/end cap by construction."* D15's shed
keys on `start_cap`/`end_cap`, **D18 makes both false at a corner**, and what actually kept the
defaults clean was `justify = "center"`. `Evenly Justify = From the end` on a 12.161 m leg drove
the evenly post 0.061 m INTO the mitered corner post. **D269 makes the claim true** by guarding a
`trim` reservation the same way — with the one documented exception of `Adjust to End`, which
deliberately lands the last anchor on the end. See §28.7 F1.

Measured on the shipped asset, both corner modes, 12 × 8 m rectangle and the 10 × 6 m L:

* **miter** — corner: two mated `corner_post` halves and nothing else; its neighbours on both legs
  are panels. One pillar.
* **bend** — no corner assembly exists at all (D36 welds the ring), the panel wraps the vertex, and
  the evenly post rides it. One pillar, never two.
* **run ends** — `start`/`end` post, then a panel. The 0.12 m doubling is gone.

**D267 — `double_pillar_m`, the check that would have caught it** (`checks.single_pillar`). Two
ideas, and both are needed:

1. **UPRIGHT is geometry, not a name** — height ≥ 3 × the widest footprint side. `post` scores
   10.0, `corner_post` 8.1, `panel` 0.48, `gate` 0.66; the threshold is not tuned, it is a gulf.
2. **A RESERVED SLOT MAY NOT BE DOUBLED BY ANOTHER SLOT** — `corner`, `start`, `end`, `evenly` and
   `marker:<id>` each exist to put ONE piece at one place. A touching cluster of uprights drawn
   from more than one slot is the defect; the number is how much wider the cluster is than its own
   widest member, in metres.

Idea 2 is what keeps it honest on the runs that are *supposed* to be a row of pillars: 270 butted
posts on the hill cases are all slot `default` (one deliberate rhythm) and the two mitered halves
of a corner post are both slot `corner` (one assembly), while the shipped defect is `corner` +
`default` and measures **0.111698 m**.

**What it cannot see, stated because the checks it joins could not see the defect it was written
for:** a *separated* double pillar (two uprights 50 mm apart read as deliberate spacing; `TOUCH_M`
is 1 mm); a MISSING pillar, an empty corner, or a corner dressed in the wrong module — it never
asks what *should* be there; doubling WITHIN one slot (two corner assemblies squeezed onto a leg
shorter than both, `AP_narrow_rect` — that is `pc_warn_overflow`'s and `corner_face_mate_m`'s job);
duplication among non-upright members (two coincident panels are invisible); a kit whose default
piece is a narrow tall pier, which its aspect rule would classify as upright; and it compares
axis-aligned world bounding boxes, so a pillar standing on a bend reads slightly wide — hence a
2 mm tolerance rather than `TOL_M`. **It is a phase-1 check only** — it is not wired into
`run_2d_checks`, because a facade's mullions are uprights in different cells by design and the rule
would need a 2D reading before it means anything there.

**Three registered mutations, every one run through `run_mutation_registry.py` and reported
`[ok] RED` against a green control export.**

| id | runner | kills | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default_slot_composed_again` | `hda` | `starter_fence_one_pillar_miter` | **0.111698 m**, 4 mixed-slot groups; reddens exactly 1 check name and nothing else |
| `evenly_doubles_the_fill` | `hda` | `starter_fence_one_pillar_bend` + `_miter` | **11.975 m** bend, **12.0 m** miter |
| `corner_style_composed_default` | `scene` | `double_pillar_m` | **19 cases red**, `V_rect_miter` at **0.111698 m** |

⚠️ **The second one exists because the `bend` row would otherwise be unfailable, and that is worth
saying out loud rather than leaving as a green.** `starter_fence_one_pillar_bend` cooks a CLOSED
rectangle: bend mode places no corner assembly (D36 welds the ring) and a closed run has no
start/end cap, so **no reserved slot exists for the fill to double** and `default_slot_composed_again`
leaves that row at 0.0 by construction. `evenly_doubles_the_fill` makes the FILL the rhythm element
as well as the `evenly` slot (`Repeating Pieces = post` with `Evenly Spaced Piece` still `post`) —
which is exactly what an artist does the first time they type `post` into Repeating Pieces without
clearing the evenly slot — and both rows go red.

The first is the exact source-level undo of D266 (with the asset rebuilt). The third composes
`cases.corner_style` the way the page used to — i.e. it applies the fixture gap of §28.1(c) — and
reddens `AA_reflex_miter`, `AB_fillet`, `AC_degenerate_corner`, `AH_sharp_turn`, `AI_triangle`,
`AJ_reflex_closed`, `AK_pentagon`, `AL_crest_corner`, `AM_graded_corner`, `AP_narrow_rect`,
`AR_offset_past`, `BI_conform_corner`, `CD_replace_bent`, `CJ_bend_butt_120`, `T_lshape_bend`,
`U_lshape_miter`, `V_rect_miter`, `W_corner_offset_pos`, `X_corner_offset_neg`.

⚠️ `default_slot_composed_again` reddens **only the `miter` row**, and that is correct rather than a
weak pairing: `bend` places no corner assembly, so there is no reserved pillar to double and
`starter_fence_one_pillar_bend` stays 0.0 on the mutated build (measured). It reddens **nothing**
in `run_scene_checks`, which is §28.1(c) restated as a number.

**D268 — a cost fixture states its composition instead of inheriting the parm defaults.** Three
cost tables read the shipped asset *at defaults*, so D266 moved them without a line of kernel code
changing:

| row | before | after D266, unpinned | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output_guard_cost` straight_2km | 1.33x | **1.81x** (ceiling 1.60) | D259's per-anchor cost, now on the default path |
| `wrangle_cost_is_flat_in_piece_count` `pc_plan_solve` | 66.5 µs/piece ceiling | **87.2 µs/piece** | same |
| `bench_deform_20km` `pc_order` | 7.38 µs/piece | **14.10 µs/piece** (ceiling 12.0) | the fill lost `post`, so the 20 km ripple built **10 029** pieces instead of 20 057 while `pc_order`'s cook barely moved (147.9 → 141.4 ms) — it sorts PRIMS and the ceiling divides by PIECES |

A/B on ONE asset with only the two slot parms swapped, 2 km straight, min of 3 dirtied cooks:

```
NEW panel + evenly post      pieces=2001  output=0.1602 s  reference=0.0883 s  ratio=1.81x
OLD post panel, no evenly    pieces=1888  output=0.1105 s  reference=0.0832 s  ratio=1.33x
```

Neither ceiling was raised. A row's shape has to be the shape its ceiling was measured on — the
same rule that keeps `WRANGLE_CEILING_US` and `WRANGLE_DEFORM_CEILING_US` apart — so
`_wrangle_rig` now pins `slot_default = "post panel"` / `slot_evenly = ""`, and every
`output_guard_cost` row pins `slot_evenly = ""` before applying its own parms. **`evenly_2km`
sets it back, and `evenly_2km` IS the shipped default composition, so the default path stays
bounded — at the 2.6x ceiling D259 already justified.** It reads 1.83x.

⚠️ **AND THAT IS TRUE BUT TOO GENEROUS, in two ways (§28.7 F12/F13).** No ceiling constant was
raised — but the default composition MOVED from the row governed by 1.6x to the row governed by
2.6x, so the guard on the default path is **62 % looser** than it was. And `evenly_2km` is a
dead-flat straight line, so it bounds the default's STRAIGHT path only: the shipped default's
**deformed** path is bounded by nothing, because `_wrangle_rig` pins the old composition.

**The honest price of the fix, recorded rather than hidden:** the default cook is **+45 %** on a
2 km / 2 000-piece fence (0.1105 → 0.1602 s), and the shipped output path is 1.81x its own Python
oracle there where it was 1.33x. That is D259's per-anchor fixed cost and D260's named remedy
arriving on the default path; it is 50 ms on a 2 km fence and it buys a fence that reads correctly,
which is §6's own acceptance criterion. **It is a debt with an owner, not a surprise.**

### 28.3 The two pinned fixtures, and why they are not a fix

`DOUBLE_PILLAR` in `run_scene_checks.py` pins **`A_straight` and `DL_variant_kit` at 0.12 m** —
the run-END half of this very defect, live in the committed suite. `cases.fence_style` is the
suite's **only** coverage of the `sequence` selector, and rewriting it deletes that fixture; and a
live instance of the defect inside the suite is the standing proof this check can see one — the
value is exactly the post width, so a check that quietly stopped measuring would drop to 0.0 and go
red there. The shipped defaults no longer do this; `run_hda_checks` and `gate_images` drive the
parm face and assert 0.0. (⚠️ The `gate_images` half of that sentence was **false when it was
written** — that file ran nine checks over PC-G1 and `single_pillar` was not one of them. It is
true now; §28.7 F5.) A third entry, `ED_rect_evenly_adjust`, joined the table at D269 — see §28.7.

| `tests/unit/test_polychain*.py`, `test_plan.py` | OK |
| `run_scene_checks.py` | **0 failing, 0 moved** |
| `run_2d_checks.py` | **0 failing, 0 moved** |
| `run_native_checks.py` | **0 failing** |
| `run_hda_checks.py` | **0 failing** (2 new rows) |

| `scale_gate.py` | 0 failing rows |
| `gate_images.py` | **0 failing gate checks**, 19 images |

`baseline.json`'s diff is **purely additive**: one `double_pillar_m` row per case, plus one changed

baselined VALUE moved anywhere in the tree — the parm-face change reaches no scene case, because
every scene case builds its style in Python. That is the fixture gap of §28.1(c), visible one last
time as an absence.

⚠️ **Two timing checks failed once each and passed on re-run, on a machine with another agent's
`hython` and Hannes' `houdinifx` both live**: `solve_cost_is_flat_in_piece_count` at 0.551 against
a 0.55 calibrated ceiling (0.2 % over — the check's own docstring records why that constant became
a calibrator), and the two D268 rows *before* they were pinned. The D268 rows had a real cause and
were fixed at the fixture; the solve row is contention and is recorded as such rather than
re-ceilinged.

### 28.5 Decisions

- **D266 — the shipped default composition is RailClone's canonical fence: panels fill the run,
  posts are Evenly-spaced at 2 m.** A composed fill cannot avoid doubling the piece at one end of
  every run, because an alternating unit of even period opens and closes with different members.
  The rhythm element belongs in a slot whose anchors are clear of the run's ends by construction.
- **D267 — composition is asserted as "a touching group of uprights drawn from more than one slot
  is a defect", and its size is how much wider that group is than its own widest member.** Names
  are not a vocabulary a check may depend on; geometry and slot are.
- **D268 — a cost fixture states the composition its ceiling was measured on.** A fixture that
  reads the parm defaults silently re-measures itself every time an artist-facing default changes,
  and the only two outcomes are a false failure or a loosened ceiling.
- **FINDING (no D, because nothing was built for it) — the engine cannot phase a composed unit
  against what a neighbouring assembly supplied.** No phase on `sequence`, no ctx subject for
  "this run is already capped". §28.1(b) has the shape of the fix if it is ever wanted.

### 28.6 What this cycle did NOT do

- ⚠️ **Dev-loop rule 0 was NOT discharged when this was written, and §28.7 is what discharged it.**
  The three things this bullet told an auditor to attack were the right three: the aspect-ratio
  classifier on a kit that is not the starter fence was **two separate defects** (F2's false
  negative on a blocky corner, F3's false positive on a dense picket spacing), the pinned
  `DOUBLE_PILLAR` entries survived the metric rewrite unchanged and were **not** over-reach, and
  `evenly_spacing = 2.0` remains open (§28.8 item 4). Fifteen findings in total; §28.7 has them.
- `run_2d_checks` does not run `double_pillar_m` (see §28.2).
- D259/D260 are not paid down; D266 merely moved their cost onto the default path.

### 28.7 The audit of §28, worked through (2026-08-24)

**Dev-loop rule 0, discharged for §28.** Fifteen findings from an agent that did not write it,
every one reproduced from a pristine export before it was touched. Three of them said the same
thing in three different places: *the check written to see a double pillar could not see one on
any kit but the starter fence.*

**F1 — the stated mechanism of D266 was FALSE, and the false sentence SHIPPED.** §28.2 claimed
D15's half-module shed keeps an evenly anchor clear of a corner "by construction", and
`slot_evenly`'s own help string on the built asset said "a corner or cap piece is never doubled by
one of these". Neither was true. `plan.plan_section` builds `head`/`tail` from
`section.start_cap`/`end_cap`, and **D18 makes both FALSE at a corner** — a corner reserves its
space through `trim`, not through a cap — so the shed never ran there at all. What actually kept
the shipped defaults clean was `justify = "center"`, whose lead is `(L-(n-1)d)/2` and therefore at
least half a spacing: an accident of one default, not a guarantee. **One Advanced parm reached the
defect this cycle exists to fix.** Reproduced on the shipped asset, miter, starter kit, nothing but
a curve wired:

| parm | leg | `double_pillar_m` before | after D269 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Evenly Justify = From the end` | 12.161 m | **0.061** | **0.0** |
| " | 12.17 / 12.18 / 12.20 / 12.25 m | 0.07 / 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.15 | **0.0** |
| `Evenly Justify = From the start` | 12.161 m | 0.061, at the trailing end | **0.0** |
| `Adjust to End = 1.0` | 4.66 / 6.66 / 8.66 / 12.66 / 12.70 / 12.90 m | **0.06 at every corner** | 0.12, abutting |

**D269 sheds the clearance at any RESERVED boundary, not only at a capped one** — `trim[0] > 0` /
`trim[1] > 0` earn the same half-module + pad set-back that a cap gets. Two lines. The 0.061 m the
justify cases lost was **interpenetration**: the evenly post stood half inside the corner post.

⚠️ **`Adjust to End` is NOT taken to zero, and that is a decision rather than a residue.** The parm
means *land the last anchor exactly on the section end*, and at a corner that end carries the
corner post. After D269 the interpenetration is gone and what remains is an exact abutment — one
whole 0.12 m post, zero overlap. Engineering that away would be overriding an instruction the
artist typed. So it is **pinned** (`ED_rect_evenly_adjust` in the scene suite,
`evenly_clears_the_corner_adjust_to_end` in `run_hda_checks`) and both parm help strings now say
what is true instead of what was hoped: `slot_evenly` promises *half a module clear … except where
Adjust to End is on*, and `adjust_to_end` warns that the last piece will stand against a corner or
a cap.

⚠️ **THE LEG LENGTH IS HALF THE FIXTURE.** On the 12 × 8 m rectangle every justification measures
0.0 **both before and after** D269 — 12 m is an exact multiple of the 2 m spacing, so the justify
leftover never approaches zero and the defect is unreachable there. A fixture on the round number
is green on the broken build. `RECT_ODD` is 12.161 × 8.161 m for that reason, and the registered
mutation `evenly_ignores_the_corner_reserve` records it as its own second half.

**F2 / F3 / F9 / F8 — `single_pillar` was four different wrong checks, and D270 rewrote it.** Each
was measured, not argued.

| what was wrong | measured on the old check | after D270 |
|---|---|---|
| **F2, false NEGATIVE.** `_is_upright` gated *entry*, so a corner module that is not slender was never protected at all. The starter kit's own `corner_block` (1.20 × 1.30 × 0.16 m, aspect 1.08) is such a piece — and so is every plinth, pier cap and wall return, i.e. most real kits. | same build, only the corner module swapped: `corner_post` **0.111698, ok=False**; `corner_block` **0.0, ok=True** (its 8 pieces not counted at all) | `corner_block` **0.110491, ok=False**. A RESERVED piece is protected whatever its aspect; the aspect rule now only decides whether the *neighbour* is a doubler |
| **F3, false POSITIVE, non-monotonic.** The aspect was read off the PLACED world box, so the fitting solve decided the classification: adaptive fill shrinks the 2 m `panel` below 0.30 m long and its 0.90 m height then clears 3:1. | `evenly_spacing` sweep, shipped defaults otherwise, miter 12 × 8: 0.30 → **11.98**, 0.35 → 11.90, 0.40 → 11.88, 0.42 → 0.28, 0.45 → 0.28, 0.50 → 0.0, 0.60 → **0.28**, 0.80 → 0.0, 1.00 → 0.0 | **0.0 at every one of the nine.** Aspect is read off `pc_local`, the module's own space, so `fill`, `padding` and `evenly_spacing` cannot reclassify anything |
| **F9, the metric degenerated.** A transitive touching CLUSTER's span minus its widest member IS the run length once the fill is uprights and the ends are capped. | `Repeating Pieces = post`: **1999.880005 m** on a 2 km run, 11.975 / 12.0 m on PC-G1 — the registered mutation's own headline numbers were run lengths | **0.12 m**, one post, on both. The value is the worst single protected-vs-upright PAIR, per horizontal axis, bounded by one module's footprint by construction |
| **F8, cost.** The union-find swept every pair. | 3 333 uprights **0.686 s**; 16 667 uprights **33.938 s** | footprints bucketed on a grid of side `max_footprint + TOUCH_M`: 16 667 uprights in **0.108 s**, 314× |

The three pinned `DOUBLE_PILLAR` values are **unchanged** by the rewrite — `A_straight` and
`DL_variant_kit` still read exactly 0.12 — which is the evidence that the new metric measures the
same thing on the cases it was calibrated on.

⚠️ **F3's fix had to be checked on the DEFORMED branch, because that is where a local-space read
could have been empty.** `place` writes `pc_local` for every non-packed piece — anchored, mitered
and deformed alike (`place.py` sets it AFTER the transform, precisely so a rotated local frame
cannot leak the world in) — but nothing said so. Measured on a 40 m sine hill, `panel` fill +
`evenly post`, spacing 0.30 / 0.35 / 0.50 / 1.00 / 2.00 m: **137 of 275 elements are multi-prim
deformed pieces, the upright set is `['post']` at every spacing, and `double_pillar_m` is 0.0 at
every spacing.** On the old placed-box rule the same run at 0.30 m would have called every panel
an upright.

**F4 — the fixture gap was INVERTED, not closed, and that is the finding that stings.** §28.1(c)
diagnosed the original defect as *"the one composition the parameter page actually shipped was in
no corner case in the suite"* — and after D266 that sentence was **still true, of the new
defaults**. `grep -c evenly tests/polychain/cases.py` returned **0**. The ~35 corner and closure
checks were once again running a composition the asset does not ship, and the only assertion on
the new defaults was two rows of `run_hda_checks` on one rectangle: the same one-fixture shape
that let the original defect ship, one cycle later. **Nine cases close it** (EA–EI): the shipped
composition through the whole corner battery on a rectangle, an L, a reflex zigzag and a pentagon;
all three justifications and `adjust_to_end` on `RECT_ODD`; **EH**, the blocky corner module F2
could not see; and **EI**, a marker slot on a cornered curve, which no marker case had ever reached
(T2/T3/D/N all run straight curves with no corner rule).

**F5 — a comment that made one fixture look like two.** `run_scene_checks`'s `DOUBLE_PILLAR` block
said "`run_hda_checks.py` and `gate_images.py` drive the parm face and assert 0.0 there".
`gate_images` ran nine checks over PC-G1 and `single_pillar` was not one of them — all nine were
closure checks, which is precisely the family that cannot see this defect. It is there now, so the
parm face is asserted over the L and the **3 m close-up** as well as the rectangle.

**F6 / F10 / F11 — three blind spots the docstring got wrong or did not state.** `_touching`'s Y
clause was credited with stopping a finial stacked on a post reading as a second pillar; it is an
overlap test with 1 mm slack, so an exactly-stacked finial passes it — what actually makes a
concentric stack score zero is the `span − own` form of the metric (measured: 0.0). The rule flags
**any** upright from another slot touching a reserved piece, **including the lamp-on-a-bollard
composition `slot_evenly`'s own help advertises** (measured 0.08 m, red — `expected` is the escape
hatch). And the 2 mm `tol` is a dead zone in both directions: 0.0015 and 0.0019 pass, 0.0021 fails.
All three are in the check's "what it cannot see" block now.

**F7 — the mutation registry's control build could invalidate a sweep silently.** It reported
`hda 33 checks, 1 red` on a pristine HEAD export, aborted the whole sweep, **did not name the
row**, then ran green on re-run and green again when the export was reproduced by hand. The
control now prints its failing check names and re-runs once before declaring itself broken.

**F12 / F13 / F14 — three claims in this section that were too generous, corrected in place.**

- The `_wrangle_rig` pin's comment said the shipped default's cost is bounded by `evenly_2km` in
  `output_guard_cost`. `evenly_2km` is `guard_polyline_geo([(1.0*i, 0, 0) …])`, a dead-flat line
  that never enters the deform branch — so it bounds the shipped default's **straight** path and
  the shipped default's **deformed** path has no committed ceiling. Standing finding §28.8(3),
  not closed with a ceiling calibrated on a contended machine.
- No `*_CEILING_*` constant was raised (verified by diff), but the default composition **moved from
  the row governed by 1.6x to the row governed by 2.6x**. §28.2's "the default path stays bounded —
  at the 2.6x ceiling D259 already justified" reads cost-neutral and is not: the guard on the
  default path is **62 % looser** than it was, and paying down D259's per-anchor cost now buys back
  a *default-path* ceiling rather than an opt-in one.
- D266 is a **defaults change**, so `pc_elem_id` addresses on the default asset move (bend 38 → 39
  pieces, miter → 44). 3.4's "ids are structural and must survive" governs refactors, not
  deliberate composition changes — but 4.6's override cascade keys on `pc_elem_id`, so **an
  override payload written against the pre-D266 defaults must be re-addressed** and will otherwise
  miss silently. No code change; recorded so it is not rediscovered.

**AND THE SWEEP FOUND ONE MORE, which is the meta-runner doing its job rather than a reviewer.**
`run_mutation_registry.py --runner hda` reported **`kit_input_unplugged` SURVIVED — "still green:
`input2_is_the_kit`; what it DID redden (0): nothing at all"**. The asset's kit port wired to
NOTHING changed no check. Thirty of the thirty-one legitimately cannot tell (they wire no kit, and
3.4's `kit_starter` supplies the same starter kit either way); the one written to tell could not
fail, because it asserted a NAME. `Kit.resolve` ends `return [stand_in(name)]`, so a module the kit
cannot supply becomes a **blank 1 × 1 × 1 box carrying the requested name** — `plank` appears in
`pc_module` whether input 2 was read or not. The previous cycle recorded the mechanism correctly
and left it (*"`run_hda_checks.py` is not this cycle's file to edit"*); **D272** closes it, because
this cycle was already editing that file for D269. It asserts the renamed module's own geometry off
`pc_local` — 2.00 × 0.90 × 0.06 m, the panel, against the stand-in's 1 × 1 × 1 — and the mutation
reddens it. Retrospective 4a rule 4, *assert truth, not presence*, caught by a sweep and not by a
reading.

### 28.8 Standing findings — open, named, not implied

1. **The engine cannot phase a composed unit against what a neighbouring assembly supplied.**
   Unchanged from §28.5, restated here because it is the answer to "why is the fix in the style and
   not in the engine". `plan.choose` resolves a `sequence` as `cand[index % len(cand)]` and
   `plan_section` starts every section's fill at `index = 0`; there is no phase field on `Rule`,
   and `plan.cond_subject` has no subject for *"the head of this run is already capped"*
   (`cornerAngle` is a different fact — the section's own turn, not what the neighbour supplied).
   So a style that wants `post panel` **and** one pillar at a corner is inexpressible today.
   The shape of the fix if it is ever wanted: a `phase` field on `Rule` and a `section_capped`
   ctx subject. Nothing in §28 depends on it — the `evenly` slot is the general answer to "rhythm
   element" and it is the one RailClone reaches for.
2. **A marker landing inside a corner assembly's reserve shares ground with it.** `trim` belongs to
   the corner alone; nothing reserves space for a `marker:<id>` anchor against it. Measured on the
   L with the marker 0.4 m short of the vertex: `pc_warn_overflow`, `corner_abut_m` **0.040**,
   `corner_face_mate_m` **0.113**, `double_pillar_m` **0.0767** (`marker:7:gate` +
   `corner:corner_post`). The engine warns rather than blocks, which is D13's policy working — but
   the seam does open. `EI_marker_at_corner` runs the marker mid-leg deliberately and records the
   collision numbers in a comment rather than pinning them, because closing it that way would mean
   giving `corner_abut` an `expected` for a fixture's convenience.
3. **The shipped default's DEFORMED path has no cost ceiling.** F12 above.
4. **`evenly_spacing = 2.0` is the starter panel's own length, not a general answer.** A kit whose
   panel is not 2 m gets a rhythm that does not land on its joints. Carried over from §28.6.

### 28.9 Decisions

- **D269 — a RESERVED boundary is guarded, not only a CAPPED one.** D15's half-module shed keyed on
  `start_cap`/`end_cap`, and D18 makes both false at a corner, so the guarantee the parm help
  advertised did not exist: `justify = "center"` was providing it by accident. Anything that
  reserves span — a cap through `head`/`tail`, a corner assembly through `trim` — earns the same
  set-back. `adjust_to_end` still lands on the guarded end, because that is what the parm means,
  and the help now says so.
- **D270 — a check may not let one geometric rule decide both what it protects and what counts as
  a doubler, and it may not read a quantity the pipeline downstream of it can change.** Protection
  follows the SLOT (structural, unchangeable by a fit); doubling follows the ASPECT of the module's
  OWN geometry (`pc_local`, before placement). Reading the placed box let `evenly_spacing = 0.35`
  report an 11.9 m double pillar on an ordinary picket fence; gating entry on the aspect let a
  blocky corner double forever at 0.0. The value is pairwise, so it is a pillar width and never a
  run length, and the sweep is bucketed, so it is linear.
- **D272 — a check on "the right module arrived" asserts the module's GEOMETRY, never its name.**
  `Kit.resolve`'s stand-in is a blank box that carries the requested name, by design (3.4:
  warn-never-block), so any assertion phrased as *"`plank` appears in `pc_module`"* is satisfied by
  the failure it exists to catch. Read `pc_local` and compare the module's own extents.
- **D271 — a fixture's own dimensions are part of the fixture.** Every justification measures 0.0
  on a 12 m leg at 2 m spacing whether the engine is fixed or broken, because 12 is a multiple of
  2. The round number is what a fixture author reaches for and it is exactly the number that cannot
  fail. A fixture for a leftover-driven defect must be built on a length that leaves a leftover.
